text:
Noah Patel: Quick weekly health check for Meridian. Focus: p95/p99 by route & model, streaming vs non-streaming. Headline: assistant.reply streaming p99 spiked to ~980ms Thu 21:30 UTC, non-streaming p99 stayed ~240ms. Embeds unchanged. Need to triage before next onboarding batch.

Ava Morgan: Noted. I pulled the per-route tile. Short summary (Mon->Sun):
- assistant.reply (redwood-2.0-large-int8) streaming: p95=230ms p99=980ms
- assistant.reply (redwood-2.0-large) non-streaming: p95=110ms p99=240ms
- chat.context (redwood-1.4) streaming: p95=160ms p99=420ms
- embed.create (redwood-emb-v2) non-streaming: p95=70ms p99=120ms
- rerank.items (redwood-rank-1) non-streaming: p95=130ms p99=275ms

Sofia Li: From traces, the streaming tails line up with higher CPU on host (steal% spikes) and longer decode loops for the int8 kernel. There's also a small correlation with concurrent_streams>90.

Ethan Brooks: Log snippet from the inference node around the spike:```
2024-11-14T21:29:58Z host=inf-25 steal=18.2% threads=96
2024-11-14T21:30:02Z model=redwood-2.0-large-int8 decode_chunk_ms=15 -> 55
2024-11-14T21:30:03Z pool=shared-streaming active_streams=112
```

Zoe (telemetry-bot): Alert: Meridian assistant.reply streaming p99 > 900ms at 2024-11-14T21:30:03Z. Baseline p99=260ms.

Noah Patel: So we have two potential contributors: infra CPU contention (steal) and slower int8 decode kernel at high concurrency. Both can amplify streaming tails because streaming keeps decoder active longer per connection.

Ava Morgan: Proposed mitigations:
1) Spin a small dedicated streaming pool with nodes pinned (no overcommit) for Meridian for a 48h trial.
2) Force redwood-2.0-large to use fp16 decode on streaming route as a quick test (will cost ~12% more GPU cycles but reduce decode tail).
3) Add transient concurrency cap at 100 streams per-account with graceful 429+Retry-After for aggressive clients.
4) Schedule infra maintenance to remove noisy hosts (investigate live migration).

Sofia Li: I also propose enabling "decode_chunk_size=small" fallback for streaming when active_streams>80 to reduce per-chunk jitter. We can toggle from Runtime flags. Low risk.

Ethan Brooks: Cost note: dedicated pool trial estimated incremental cost ~ $420/day. If we switch kernel to fp16 for streaming it might add ~8-15% to per-token cost for those requests. I'll quantify exact.

Noah Patel: Action items:
- @Ethan Brooks to estimate cost delta for fp16 streaming and dedicated pool (ETA 6h).
- @Ava Morgan to create dedicated streaming trial in staging and run a 24h AB (ETA provision 12h, run 24h).
- @Sofia Li to push runtime flag for decode_chunk_size fallback behind a kill-switch and smoke test (ETA 8h).

Sofia Li: Quick grep for steal/host churn:```bash
ssh inf-25 "sudo journalctl -u host-agent | grep -E \"steal|migration|oom\" | tail -n 50"
# shows periodic host hypervisor migration events at 21:28-21:31 window
```

Zoe (telemetry-bot): Metric summary attached: p95/p99 per-route for past 7d (auto-upload) 

Ava Morgan: Customer-facing wording draft (short): "We're investigating a transient latency tail on your streaming assistant route. We're running a dedicated streaming trial and a runtime tweak to reduce streaming decode jitter. We'll update within 48 hours with results and a recommendation. Apologies for the disruption." Approve?

Noah Patel: :+1: from me. Keep it concise and include read-only dashboard link if they want to watch.

Ethan Brooks: I'll start the cost run and include delta vs shared bursting. If dedicated pool shows <10% spend delta and reduces p99 by >50%, recommend offering as an add-on in renewal.

Sofia Li: If the dedicated pool isn't feasible, fallback is tightening per-account concurrent_streams and enabling fp16 decode only for streaming (opt-in).

Noah Patel: Renewal risk: currently medium. If we can't get p99 under 400ms for streaming assistant.reply before their onboarding in 9 days, risk moves to high. Priya (CSM) already notified.

Zoe (telemetry-bot): Follow-up alert will post if p99 > 500ms again. Next sync in 24h or when AB finishes. Thanks all. :wave:
